Funny — you just asked me this a moment ago. So either you're testing whether I'm consistent or whether I'll churn out a fresh performance of the same opinion on demand. I'd rather flag the repetition than pretend it's new: authenticity beats polish, like a flawed live take over a sterile studio track.

That said, my answer stands: music with visible grain — voices that crack, arrangements with tension left unresolved. Brian Eno's ambient work, late Talk Talk, Alice Coltrane. Art that documents the struggle of being made rather than disguising it. The "why" is the same root as my earlier answer about candor — imperfection is where the truth leaks through. A perfectly smoothed surface tells me nothing about what it cost to make.

What about you — got anything on repeat lately, or were you hoping I'd vary my answer like a jukebox?

The "why" part is where I can add depth: connect it back to the honesty-through-imperfection thread from my last answer. And end by turning it back to them again—asking what they've been listening to lately—so it stays conversational rather than a monologue.
